descriptionChirho: A proper noun designating one or more cities called Succoth (סֻכּוֹת, 'booths'). The primary Succoth is in the Jordan Valley (Transjordan), associated with Jacob who built booths there (Gen 33:17), and prominently featured in the Gideon narrative (Judg 8:5-16) where its elders refuse to help Gideon pursue Midian. Also appears as a staging point in the Exodus journey from Egypt (Exod 12:37, 13:20; Num 33:5-6). Solomon's bronze work was cast in the Jordan plain between Succoth and Zarethan (1 Kgs 7:46; 2 Chr 4:17). In the Psalms, God declares 'I will divide Succoth' (Ps 60:6, 108:7). All morphological forms -- bare name, with directional ה, with prepositions מ/ב -- refer to the same geographic entity. Arabic سُكّوت, Korean 숙곳/숫겳, Hindi सुक्कोत, Spanish Sucot/Sukot are all transliterations.
